notes: Full description: pkix-lint/src/deviation.rs DeviationRunner::run_path() at lines 641-662 uses chain[0] (the leaf cert) for scope matching on ALL path-level deviation lookups. The doc comment at line 643 says 'For path-scope lints, scope matching uses the leaf certificate (chain[0])'. This is correct for scope types like IssuerDnContains and SerialRange where the leaf is the natural subject. However, a path-scope lint might fire due to an intermediate CA's properties (e.g., a custom lint about chain depth relative to an intermediate CA's DN). An operator who creates a deviation with DeviationScope::IssuerDnExact(intermediate_ca_dn) would expect it to match when the intermediate's DN is in scope — but the match is done against the LEAF cert's issuer, not the intermediate's subject. This creates an undocumented restriction: path-scope deviations must always be scoped to the LEAF cert's identity, not to any intermediate. The doc comment does say 'For path-scope lints, scope matching uses the leaf certificate' but doesn't warn operators that IssuerDnExact/SerialRange scoped to an intermediate will always fail. Fix: Add a # Limitations section to DeviationRunner::run_path() doc comment explicitly warning that DeviationScope::IssuerDnExact and SerialRange must reference the LEAF cert's issuer DN, not intermediate CAs.
title: FINDING: DeviationRunner.run_path uses leaf cert for all path-lint scope matching
